report.tagline: Meta's text-first social app, built on Instagram accounts, for short posts and public conversations.
report.simpleSummary: Threads is like Twitter, but made by Meta and connected to your Instagram account. You write short posts, reply, repost and follow people, and the app shows you a feed of posts from people you follow and others it thinks you will like. It launched in July 2023 and got 100 million sign-ups in five days because Instagram users could join in one tap. It is free, and Meta now shows ads in it.

overview.whatItDoes: Threads is a public conversation app. Users post text (with photos, videos and links), reply, quote and follow topics and communities. It is run by the Instagram team and uses Instagram accounts and follower lists to get started.
howItWorks: Users sign in with their Instagram account and can follow the same people in one tap.
The 'For You' feed recommends posts using Meta's ranking AI; a 'Following' feed shows only accounts you follow.
People post short text, add tags for topics, join interest communities and send DMs.
Threads connects to the fediverse, so some posts can be seen on apps like Mastodon.
Meta shows ads in the feed, sold through the same tools advertisers use for Instagram and Facebook.
overview.valueProposition: A friendlier, less toxic place for public conversation, with your Instagram friends and creators already there.

painPoints.pain: Starting a new social app means an empty feed and no followers.
painPoints.howSolved: Instagram login and one-tap follow of Instagram contacts.

painPoints.pain: X felt toxic and unstable for many users and advertisers.
painPoints.howSolved: Stricter moderation and a calmer tone.

painPoints.pain: Brands needed a safe text platform.
painPoints.howSolved: Meta's ad tools with brand safety controls.

businessModel.summary: Threads makes money from ads, sold through Meta's existing ad system. Ads started in 2025, and revenue is still small compared with Instagram, but Meta can add Threads to existing advertisers' campaigns with one click.

revenueStreams.detail: Image, video and carousel ads in the feed.
Advertisers add Threads to their Instagram and Facebook campaigns.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. Ads bought by auction through Meta Ads Manager.
costDrivers: Promotion inside Instagram (free for Meta but takes space)
businessModel.unitEconomics: Rough estimate. Threads shares Meta's servers, ad tools and moderation, so each extra user costs little. If Threads earns a few dollars per daily user a year today, far below Instagram's roughly $23 per user, it is still likely near break-even or better at Meta's scale. The real bet is future revenue as ad load rises.

howTheyGetUsers: Users leaving X after policy changes
growth.moat: Threads sits on top of Instagram's 3 billion users and Meta's ad system. No new app can borrow a social graph that big. Its weakness is that text conversations depend on real-time news and active posters, where X still leads.

improvementIdeas.idea: Live events hub for cricket, elections and big news
improvementIdeas.expectedImpact: More daily use and posts during events.

improvementIdeas.problem: Journalists and desk workers use X on web.
Indian users find little local content.

pmLessons: Distribution can solve the cold-start problem. Threads borrowed Instagram's network to avoid an empty app.
Sign-ups are not retention. Threads got 100 million sign-ups but had to work hard to keep people.
A competitor's mistakes create openings, but you still need a better product to keep users.
Web matters for news and work users, even in a mobile-first world.

interviewQuestions.question: How did Threads solve the cold-start problem, and what are the risks of that approach?
interviewQuestions.hint: Explain Instagram login and follow import; risks include low engagement and dependence on Instagram.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you increase posting on Threads?
interviewQuestions.hint: Find barriers, suggest prompts and communities, track posting rate.

interviewQuestions.question: Threads has more mobile users than X but far fewer web users. What would you do?
interviewQuestions.hint: Segment users, find who uses web (journalists, workers), improve web product, track web DAU.

interviewQuestions.question: When should Threads increase ad load?
interviewQuestions.hint: Use retention and engagement guardrails, test by market, compare revenue gain with user loss.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star for Threads?
interviewQuestions.hint: Daily users who post or reply, broken into users, posting rate, feed quality and ads.
